models_evaluated: MHRN primary care suicide risk model (LASSO logistic regression)
Vanderbilt University (VU) random forest suicide risk model

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of existing suicide risk models on local IHS historical data versus reference outcomes
links.effect: MHRN AUROC 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85) vs VU 0.68 (0.64-0.72) for 90-day attempts; Spiegelhalter z -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN), both P<.001, before recalibration.
links.quote: Although the generalization of the MHRN models is notable, all models were poorly calibrated initially, demonstrating the importance of recalibration when applying models to new populations.

links.outcome: Calibration before and after local recalibration with isotonic regression
links.effect: Spiegelhalter z was -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN) before; after isotonic recalibration cross-validated z was 0.18 (P=.86) for VU and 0.19 (P=.85) for MHRN.
links.quote: After recalibration using isotonic regression, the cross-validated Spiegelhalter z score was 0.18 ( P = .86) for the VU and 0.19 ( P = .85) for the MHRN primary care model.

links.outcome: Comparison of development sample populations with the local American Indian deployment population
links.effect: VU validation sample reported no American Indian/Alaska Native patients; MHRN validation had 1.1% AI/AN visits vs 94.0% in the analytic sample; only 4 of top 10 VU features and 5 of top 10 MHRN features remained top 10.
links.quote: In comparison, the validation sample for the VU model did not report any American Indian or Alaska Native patients (2080 of 77 973 patients [2.7%] are reported as other race) and reported 85 of 77 973 patients (0.1%) with an attempt included in the analysis.

links.outcome: Model performance when extended to new population (majority American Indian)
links.effect: MHRN AUROC 0.81 for 90-day attempts and 0.86 for death, but VU only 0.68 and 0.63; all models poorly calibrated initially.
links.quote: The MHRN model was significantly more accurate than the VU model.

links.outcome: ML models compared with existing screening on the same local data (AUROC)
links.effect: 90-day attempt AUROC: MHRN 0.81, VU 0.68, existing screening 0.66; screening identified no suicide deaths (sensitivity 0.0%) while MHRN AUROC for death was 0.86.
links.quote: Our results show that the machine learning models used in this study had substantially higher AUROC values than existing approaches, even when compared with a substantial uptick in ASQ administration (eTable 5 in Supplement 1 ).

links.outcome: Performance variation across visit years within a single site
links.effect: Performance for all models differed significantly by visit year; existing screening and MHRN improved each year, VU peaked in 2019.
links.quote: Performance for all models differed significantly by visit year, with estimated performance improving each year for the existing screening and the MHRN model and having the highest performance in 2019 for the VU model (eTable 4 in Supplement 1 ).

links.outcome: Calibration of models applied to new population
links.effect: Spiegelhalter z scores -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN), P<.001, indicating poor calibration despite reasonable AUROC.
links.quote: For the outcome of 90-day suicide attempts, the Spiegelhalter z score was −89.9 ( P < .001) for the VU model and 15.5 ( P < .001) for the MHRN primary care model.

unlisted_practices: Partnering with tribe and Indian Health Service (tribal approval, community-engaged evaluation) for model validation
Comparing feature importance rankings between original development and new population to explain performance differences

models_evaluated: Mental Health Research Network (MHRN) primary care suicide risk models
Vanderbilt University (VU) random forest suicide risk model

links.quote: The MHRN model had an AUROC value of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.77-0.85) for 90-day suicide attempts, whereas the VU model had an AUROC value of 0.68 (95% CI, 0.64-0.72), and the augmented screening indicator had an AUROC value of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.63-0.70).

links.effect: Spiegelhalter z improved from −89.9 and 15.5 (both P < .001) to 0.18 (P = .86) and 0.19 (P = .85).
links.quote: After recalibration using isotonic regression, the cross-validated Spiegelhalter z score was 0.18 ( P = .86) for the VU and 0.19 ( P = .85) for the MHRN primary care model.

links.effect: Analytic sample was 94.0% AIAN; VU validation reported no AIAN; MHRN validation had 37 717 of 3 387 741 visits (1.1%) AIAN.
links.quote: In comparison, the validation sample for the VU model did not report any American Indian or Alaska Native patients (2080 of 77 973 patients [2.7%] are reported as other race) and reported 85 of 77 973 patients (0.1%) with an attempt included in the analysis.

links.effect: Initial calibration was poor: Spiegelhalter z −89.9 (P < .001) for VU and 15.5 (P < .001) for MHRN; VU AUROC 0.68 vs MHRN 0.81.
links.quote: Although the generalization of the MHRN models is notable, all models were poorly calibrated initially, demonstrating the importance of recalibration when applying models to new populations.

models_evaluated: Mental Health Research Network (MHRN) primary care model

links.outcome: Model calibration before and after local recalibration
links.effect: Calibration was initially poor (Spiegelhalter z: VU -89.9, MHRN 15.5; P<.001) but improved after isotonic recalibration (VU z=0.18, P=.86; MHRN z=0.19, P=.85).
links.quote: After recalibration using isotonic regression, the cross-validated Spiegelhalter z score was 0.18 ( P = .86) for the VU and 0.19 ( P = .85) for the MHRN primary care model.

links.outcome: Discrimination for 90-day suicide attempts in new population
links.effect: AUROC was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.77-0.85) for MHRN and 0.68 (95% CI, 0.64-0.72) for VU.
links.quote: The VU model showed lower discrimination than the MHRN primary care model, with an AUROC value of 0.68 (95% CI, 0.64-0.72) compared with an AUROC value of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.77-0.85) for 90-day suicide attempts for the MHRN model.
